correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the finite alternating-block bijection by repeatedly removing all sinks: opposite colors cannot both contain sinks, and removing a set of one color cannot turn any vertex of that same color into a new sink. Reversal gives a canonical alternating block sequence, and all opposite-color edges must point toward the later block. For a terminal A-block the prefix EGF is Y(1+X)/(1-XY) with X=e^x-1 and Y=e^y-1, and the terminal factor is e^{zx}-1; transpose for B. These are exact for strictly positive mixed sizes. The repair also derives them from the earlier designated-sink sum and its value at z=0, independently verifying that only pure terms differ. For fixed k, marked numerators over H=1-XY are e^x Y x^k/k! and e^y X y^k/k!, versus XY(e^x+e^y) unmarked. Khera–Lundberg–Melczer give the unique varying positive critical point, strict minimality and nondegenerate smooth transfer uniformly on compact positive ratio ranges (their denominator e^{-x}+e^{-y}-1 is e^{-x-y}H). The same Gaussian and exponential factors cancel in the ratio, and XY=1 yields the reported weights and conditional truncated Poisson masses. The limiting masses sum to one, so fixed-k convergence implies total variation by truncation. Writing p=1-e^{-a} gives b=-log p and rho=L(p)/L(1-p), where L(u)=-log(1-u)/u is strictly increasing; thus the weight favors the larger side for unequal limiting ratios. A positive mixture of two exponentials k!P(S=k) with distinct bases is strictly log-convex, not geometric, proving it is not a single truncated Poisson. Equal ratios give a=b=log 2. The frozen small-instance verifier was inspected, not executed; finite counts do not certify the limit.

value.rationale: The unequal-ratio result resolves a natural question not answered by balanced symmetry: how sink class and count are jointly distributed once the sides differ. It identifies a direction of class bias, a dependence on that class, and a genuinely different marginal law rather than a change of a single Poisson parameter. The value is this complete limiting description, not the repackaging of exact finite counts or a new asymptotic method.
